extrait: The potentially historic vote at GTA 6 creators Rockstar Games on whether to seek formal union recognition has failed, the International Workers of Great Britain have announced. Around 1600 studio members cast ballots across 12th to 26th November, even as the company's open world Bonnie & Clyde 'em up released onto PlayStation and Xbox storefronts. In the end, approximately 25% of the participants voted in favour. According to the IWGB themselves, "the result does not prevent Rockstar workers from organising with the IWGB or exercising their trade union rights, but means management will not be formally committed to regular meetings with union representatives." Speaking to RPS in an emailed statement, Rockstar's head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe argued that the vote's failure "reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong." The IWGB, meanwhile, have declared that "this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for". They're going to keep mobilising for more labour power, with the failed vote now framed as a foot in the door. "Whilst we haven't emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening," reads the union statement. "People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We head from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions will lead us. "A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy," they continue. "But it's one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We'll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs." The Rockstar UK unionisation drive has been a long journey. The vote follows open confrontation between Rockstar management in the UK and IWGB-affiliated Rockstar employees working out of a private Discord server. After allegedly keeping the Discord server under surveillance for over two years, Rockstar bosses fired around 30 staff in October 2026 on charges of "gross misconduct" and breach of confidentiality. "This isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for," says the IWGB Rockstar Games Workers Union A week on from GTA 6's launch, devs at Rockstar Games have officially voted overwhelmingly against a union recognition deal, but those in favor say "we'll keep fighting." That there was a 93.2% turnout in the ballot, which began earlier this month, and of those voters, 1,163 employees voted against the deal, while 381 voted in favor. That's a split of 75.3% to 24.7%. Rockstar Games head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, says in a statement sent to GamesRadar+ that "we are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6," adding: "This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together." In a statement shared by Vertical Slice, the IWGB notes that the vote result will "not prevent Rockstar workers from organizing with the IWGB or exercising their trade union rights" in the future, "but means management will not be formally committed to regular meetings with union representatives." The IWGB Rockstar Games Workers Union also encourages those in favor of the deal not to back down, but to "double down on what we stand for." In a statement sent to GamesRadar+, it says: "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society – this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues.
